chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafiz al-Baghdady known as Ja'abi narrated that Abdullah ibn Bashir said: Al-Hasan ibn al-Zabarqan al-Moradi said: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated from Al-Ajlah, from Abil Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: I heard God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) say:

Three will come on the Day of Resurrection complaining to God, the Mighty and Majestic: The Quran, The Mosque, and The Household. The Quran will say: 'O Lord! They burned me and tore me up.' The Mosque will say: 'O Lord! They left me unused and wasted me.' And the Household will say: 'O Lord! They killed us, deported us, and scattered us.' So they will kneel on their knees for the lawsuit, and God, Glory be to His Majesty, will say to me: 'I am more worthy to do that.'

key_terms.الْعِتْرَةُ: The Household (specifically the Prophet's family, Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.لِلْخُصُومَةِ: For the lawsuit/dispute (referring to the standing before God for judgment)

ai.seo_question: What do the Quran, the Mosque, and the Household complain about on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith presents a unique eschatological triad where the Quran, the Mosque, and the Ahl al-Bayt personify their respective neglect by the Ummah, with the Household’s suffering taking precedence as the primary source of divine attention. The phrase 'I am more worthy of that' (li ana awla bi-dhalika) is interpreted by Shia scholars as God’s direct endorsement of the Ahl al-Bayt’s status, linking their historical persecution to the ultimate judgment. This narration underscores the inseparable link between preserving the Book, the Place of Worship, and the Progeny of the Prophet in maintaining the integrity of Islam.
